workflow_steps.objective: Confirm the initiative’s purpose, audiences, coalition needs, scope, constraints, success criteria, decision-makers and missing inputs.
Study stakeholder needs, the global circular-fashion landscape, cultural considerations, category conventions and comparable coalition identities.
Establish the brand platform, positioning, values, personality, accessibility commitments and design principles balancing boldness with practical partner use.
Develop meaningfully distinct strategic and visual directions covering identity character, coalition symbolism and campaign potential.
Evaluate directions against agreed criteria and obtain an explicit client choice before system development.
Incorporate stakeholder feedback into the selected direction while preserving approved strategic and visual decisions.
Define the logo, typography, colour, graphic language, imagery approach, accessibility standards, co-branding logic and governance rules.
Apply the approved system across representative campaign, partner, digital, presentation, event and communications touchpoints.
Validate consistency and accessibility, then package final identity assets, templates, application examples and usage guidance for handoff.

missing_inputs: Confirmed initiative name, naming scope and trademark or legal-clearance status
Detailed mission, theory of change, positioning, commitments and evidence supporting sustainability claims
Priority audiences, stakeholder groups, regions, languages and cultural sensitivities
Coalition governance model, partner tiers, endorsement rules and required co-branding relationships
Existing brand assets, research, messaging, campaign materials and intellectual-property constraints
Competitive and adjacent-initiative landscape to include or avoid
Required channels, applications, templates, file formats and technical specifications
Approval owners, consultation process and method for resolving conflicting stakeholder feedback
Timeline, budget, launch milestones and measurable success criteria
assumptions: The initiative requires a new global master-brand platform and visual identity rather than a refresh of an established system.
The initiative’s name will be supplied or approved separately; naming is not assumed to be part of this scope.
The identity must accommodate multiple partner brands without implying that every partner has equal authority or endorsement rights.
Campaign and partner applications will be demonstrated through representative examples rather than exhaustive production of every asset.
Environmental claims and circular-fashion terminology will require validation by the client’s subject-matter and legal reviewers.
Digital accessibility and multilingual expansion are treated as system requirements, with exact standards and languages to be confirmed.
stop_conditions: Do not begin concept exploration until the initiative’s purpose, priority audiences, decision-makers and evaluation criteria are approved.
Do not advance beyond concept exploration without an explicit human or client selection of one direction.
Pause identity-system finalization if the initiative name, trademark status, sustainability claims or coalition endorsement rules remain unresolved.
Do not expand partner applications until co-branding hierarchy, partner permissions and required use cases are approved.
Do not deliver final assets until accessibility requirements, localization scope, file formats, application list and governance guidance are validated.
Stop if stakeholder feedback materially contradicts the approved brand platform; return the conflict for strategic resolution rather than silently combining incompatible directions.
rationale: The workflow establishes shared strategy for a complex multi-stakeholder initiative before visual exploration, requires an explicit direction choice, then converts the selected concept into a governed identity system and practical campaign and partner applications. Production-specific packaging, dieline and manufacturing steps are outside the brief.
